verdict.rationale: Apify's docs describe a monitoring capability that covers all three parts of the story: checking Actor performance, validating data quality, and receiving alerts. Failure alerting is backed further by documented webhooks that fire, for example as an HTTP request to another service, when a run finishes or fails. Log streaming adds a way to observe runs. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the performance metrics and data-quality validation rules (only a one-line summary), alert channel and configuration details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can monitor job performance, validate data quality, and receive alerts when something fails

citations.quote: Check the performance of your Actors, validate data quality, and receive alerts.
you can use webhooks to start another Actor when an Actor run finishes or fails.
Webhooks provide an easy and reliable way to configure the Apify platform to carry out an action (e.g. a HTTP request to another service) when a certain system event
